page: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz, providing 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system includes 192.0 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features 2835 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity, while discrete GPU acceleration is not present on this machine type.

The x86_64 architecture incorporates per-core cache allocations of 48 KB L1 data, 1.0 MB L2, and a 32 MB L3 cache segment. Hardware support includes AVX-512 extensions (encompassing AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16) along with hardware cryptography primitives such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. These vector and cryptographic enhancements yield strong single-core compute performance, as reflected in high benchmark scores across Geekbench and single-threaded stress-ng tests.

Benchmark results highlight balanced system throughput, recording 86468.87 in multi-core stress-ng tests, 76.88 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, and 59.25 GB/sec in static web serving. While cached memory bandwidth is high, uncached large-block read bandwidth performs in the average range. The inclusion of dense local NVMe storage reduces reliance on external networked disks, improving qualitative cost efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads. The D48ads_v7 is well suited for relational databases, distributed caching layers, software compilation pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v7 is a general-purpose instance featuring 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system includes 192.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation, and integrates 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The processor incorporates AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI vector and cryptographic instruction sets, delivering strong single-thread performance alongside high multi-core throughput across Geekbench and stress-ng suites. While uncached large-block memory read bandwidth lands in the median tier, write operations and cached memory throughput remain robust. The high core density paired with bundled NVMe media delivers a balanced resource profile that lowers reliance on external storage arrays. Microsoft Azure D48ads_v7 is engineered for enterprise relational databases, Redis caching layers, continuous integration build pipelines, and CPU-driven inference tasks.
